explain.say: On a yacht on the Thames at dusk, a sailor called Marlow begins by saying that London too was once one of the dark places of the earth. Joseph Conrad published Heart of Darkness in 1899, drawing on his own trip up the Congo in 1890. A gentle note: the book shows colonial cruelty and uses racist language, and we will read it critically.

explain.say: Look at the map. Conrad's real route ran from London to Brussels, where a trading company hired him, then by sea to the mouth of the Congo and up the river by steamer. At that time the Congo was the private colony of King Leopold the Second of Belgium. Why might Conrad never name the country in the story?

draw.label: Conrad’s own 1890 journey, which Marlow’s story follows: London, Brussels, then up the Congo

explain.say: Look at the third panel. At the Outer Station Marlow sees African workers in chains and men left to die in a grove, worked to death for ivory. The Company men call this progress. Historians agree huge numbers died under Leopold's regime, with estimates running into the millions. What does the word civilising hide here?

explain.say: Here are rival readings. On the left, the novella attacks empire, showing greed dressed up as civilisation. On the right, the Nigerian novelist Chinua Achebe argued in a 1975 lecture that it reduces Africa to a dark backdrop for a European's crisis, denies Africans a voice, and is racist. Can a book attack empire and still be racist?

Marlow finally reaches Kurtz, the star ivory agent, sick and worshipped, whose report on civilising ends with a scrawled call to exterminate. Dying, Kurtz whispers: the horror, the horror. Back in Brussels, Marlow lies to Kurtz's fiancée. Well done for thinking hard. Challenge: is the horror Kurtz sees in the world, or in himself?

faq.a: An unnamed narrator on a yacht on the Thames reports the story Marlow tells, so we hear Marlow's tale at second hand. This frame lets Conrad question how much any teller understands.

faq.q: What was the Congo Free State?
faq.a: From 1885 to 1908 the Congo was the personal colony of King Leopold II of Belgium, run for ivory and later rubber through forced labour, mutilation and killing. International outrage led Belgium to take it over in 1908.
The Company's most successful ivory agent, a gifted, eloquent man who has set himself up as a god among local people and uses terror to collect ivory. Marlow is fascinated and appalled by him.

faq.q: What does The horror mean in Heart of Darkness?
faq.a: Kurtz's dying words are left open. They may judge his own crimes, the greed of empire, or the darkness Conrad suggests lies in every human heart.

faq.q: Why did Achebe call Conrad racist?
faq.a: In his 1975 lecture An Image of Africa, Achebe argued that the novella treats Africa as a setting for European self-discovery, describes Africans as barely human and gives them almost no speech. The lecture changed how the book is taught.

facts: Heart of Darkness was serialised in Blackwood's Magazine in 1899 and published as a book in 1902.
Conrad, born Józef Korzeniowski to Polish parents in 1857, learned English as a young man and captained a Congo steamer in 1890.
Chinua Achebe gave his lecture An Image of Africa in 1975; it was published in 1977.
